meta.title: Inflation Year-over-Year, 1926–2026
meta.class: Ryan Mayer · 10th-grade Economics · Battery Creek High School, SC
meta.cpiSeries: CPIAUCNS (CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted)
meta.cpiSource: FRED / U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
meta.latestNote: 2026 CPI and several sticker prices are January–July averages, not a full calendar year. Labeled YTD in the app.

goods.name: Movie ticket
goods.notes: NATO / Cinema United / The Numbers average ticket from 1948. Earlier years are theater-history averages. 2020–21 and 2025–26 are filled (COVID reporting gap; latest ticket years CPI-scaled).

goods.name: Gallon of gasoline
goods.notes: EIA / DOE historical regular retail through 1948; EIA Monthly Energy Review T09.04 annual 1949–2025 (unleaded when available, else leaded). 2026 is BLS city-average regular, January–July.

goods.name: Loaf of bread
goods.notes: BLS historical white-bread prices, then FRED APU0000702111 (1980–2025). A pound of white bread is the long-run BLS unit — roughly one loaf. 2026 is January–July average.

goods.name: Cheese pizza
goods.notes: One consistent product: a large cheese (no extra toppings) takeout pizza. There is no official century-long BLS sticker series. Anchors are industry / menu / survey averages; years between anchors are linear estimates. National averages start in 1950.
goods.unavailableReason: Pizza was not yet a typical U.S. national staple — series starts in 1950.

goods.name: Gallon of milk
goods.notes: Earlier BLS quotes were per quart or half-gallon and are converted to a gallon. FRED APU0000709112 from 1996. 2026 is January–July average.

goods.name: Pound of coffee
goods.unit: ground roast coffee, per pound (grocery — not a café cup)
goods.notes: BLS grocery ground coffee per pound, not a coffee-shop cup. Historical BLS averages through 1979; FRED APU0000717311 from 1980 (2008 interpolated). 2026 is January–July average.

goods.name: New car
goods.notes: Representative average new-vehicle price (BEA expenditure, NADA, and later KBB-style transaction averages). Mix shifts from cars toward light trucks after the 1990s. Interpolated between documented years.

goods.name: Median house
goods.unit: see note — series definition changes in 1963
goods.notes: 1940–1960: Census median value of owner-occupied homes (not sale prices). 1963–2026: FRED MSPUS median sales price of houses sold. These are related but not identical concepts. No national Census median before 1940. 2026 is Q1–Q2 average.
goods.unavailableReason: No official national median until the 1940 Census.

goods.name: Federal minimum wage
goods.notes: Fair Labor Standards Act (1938). FRED FEDMINNFRWG annual statutory rate. Context, not a grocery price. Some years are averages of mid-year statutory changes.
goods.unavailableReason: No federal minimum wage until the 1938 Fair Labor Standards Act.

episodes.label: Great Depression
episodes.headline: Prices fell — this is deflation
episodes.cue: Watch the year-over-year rate turn negative. A dollar bought more goods, but jobs and incomes collapsed. Ask: is falling prices always good news?

episodes.label: WWII & postwar
episodes.headline: Wartime demand, then a postwar jump
episodes.cue: Price controls held some stickers down during the war; when controls lifted, the CPI jumped (see 1946–48). Compare a movie ticket and a loaf of bread.

episodes.label: 1970s oil shocks
episodes.headline: Energy shocks and double-digit inflation
episodes.cue: Scrub 1973–74 and 1979. Gasoline moves first; then other prices follow. Pause on 1979 and ask what students notice in the basket.

episodes.label: Early 1980s
episodes.headline: Inflation peaks, then cools
episodes.cue: The CPI rise is still very high in 1980, then slows. This is the Volcker-era disinflation — tight money, painful unemployment, falling inflation. Stay factual; no party framing.

episodes.label: 2008–09
episodes.headline: Crisis, then a rare CPI dip
episodes.cue: 2008 energy prices spiked, then 2009 shows a slightly negative year-over-year CPI. House sale prices also fall. Compare gasoline 2008 vs 2009.

episodes.label: 2021–22
episodes.headline: A fast inflation burst
episodes.cue: After a calm 2010s, 2021–22 CPI jumps. Used cars, energy, and food led headlines. Ask which basket items moved more than the overall CPI.
